sentences.text: Shri Mohit Shivhare- GA appearing for respondents/State.

1. Heard on I.A.No.18619/2025, first application under Section 430 (1) of BNSS, 2023 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant.
2.

This appeal assails the judgment dated 08.05.2025 passed by Seventh Additional Sessions Judge,
Bhind in S.T. No. 190/2021 whereby, appellant has been convicted under Section 465 and 467 of IPC and Section 25 (1-A) of Arms Act and sentenced to undergo maximum sentence of 10 years RI with maximum fine of Rs.1,00,000/- with default stipulation.
3.

It is the case of the prosecution that on information received from the informant, the raid was conducted by the police party at the residence of the appellant on 17-07-2021 and, unauthorized possession of 32 bore country-made pistol and one magazine containing live cartridge and 13 other cartridges were recovered from the box and on being asked, the appellant failed to produce any license for the said arm.

During the search operation, in a plastic box, eight rubber stamp seals of various government offices were also recovered including the seals of Naib Tehsildar, Bhind,
Sub-Divisional Officer, Bhind, Principal, DAV Primary College Bhind, and other offices.

On the basis whereof, FIR bearing Crime No. 1/2021 was registered against the appellant at Police Station Bhind for commission 2 CRA-5951-2025 of offence under Sections 420, 465, 467, 468 of IPC and Section 25(1) (a), 25(1- B) (a), 26 and 27 of Arms Act 1959.

On completion of investigation, the charge sheet was filed in the trial court and the appellant was put to trial and vide impugned judgment dated 08.05.2025, the appellant stands convicted for the offences as stated above.
4. The learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant submits that as on date, including the custody period while on trial, the appellant has completed nearly 18 months of jail sentence.

The trial conducted against the appellant stands vitiated for want of non-compliance of principle of natural justice in as much as the right of the appellant to cross-examine the Investigating Officer Ratna Jain (PW-5), was illegally closed by the learned Trial Court vide order dated 03-03- 2025.
By referring to the evidence of PW-5, the learned senior counsel submits that the examination-in-chief of PW-5 was held on 01-06-2023.

However, the same could not be concluded on the said date as, the articles alleged to have been seized from the appellant were not produced in the court on the said date and therefore, her evidence was adjourned and recommenced on 03-03-2025 and on the very Kusum Bhadoriya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129124931/
1 same date, the right of the appellant to cross-examine her was closed.

sentences.text: That apart, he submits that the prosecution witness to the seizure namely, Smt. Neeraj (PW-3), did not entirely support the case of the prosecution.
The recovery of the seal from the appellant is not proved in accordance with law and therefore, he prays for suspension of the remaining jail sentence of the appellant.

5. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the State by referring to the reply filed to the IA for suspension of sentence opposes the application and submits that in case the appellant was aggrieved by closure of her right to cross-examine the investigating officer, the issue ought to have been taken further at the relevant stage.
However, now having failed to do so, the appellant is 3 CRA-5951-2025 not entitled to derive out any benefit on the said ground.
He further submits that the trial court has considered the material evidence brought on record and has rightly convicted the appellant, therefore, no case for suspension is made out.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties on the said IA.
7.

After taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, the period of custody and the procedure adopted by the trial court, however, without commenting on merits,
I.A.No.18619/2025 is hereby allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the entire fine amount,
if not already deposited, and on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the present appellant shall remain suspended and she be released on bail.

8. The appellant is further directed to mark her appearance before the concerned trial Court on 01.12.2026 and on such other subsequent dates as may be fixed by the said Court in this regard till final disposal of this appeal.

9. List the case for final hearing in due course.
10.
